study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Wu & Baeken, Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Sex Determines Anterior Cingulate Cortex Cortical Thickness in the Course of Depression

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study's objectives are clearly stated: to investigate sex differences in ACC cortical thickness (CT) in the course of depression (first-episode vs recurrent) and to explore lateralization. The purpose of using normative modeling ('to assess the within-group heterogeneity... capture individual-level variability') is also described.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: we first hypothesized that the ACC CT would be significantly thinner in patients experiencing relapse than in patients with first-episode MDD... we also hypothesized that these ACC CT reductions would primarily be found in the pgACC and sgACC areas... Finally, to assess the within-group heterogeneity, we also applied neuroanatomical normative modeling to capture individual-level variability in ACC CT
cm1_research_objectives.location: Main text, Introduction and Methods sections

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates (sex, age, education) were used in the normative model. Site effects were addressed using Hierarchical Bayesian regression.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Hierarchical Bayesian regression analysis was employed to accommodate intersite variation and generate normative models using the covariates of sex, age, and education.
